highlights.title: Cognition Open-Sources an Agent Plugin that Helps Secure Systems against Recent Cybersecurity Threats
highlights.contentSnippet: Cognition released the Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin, 3 MIT-licensed agent skills that inventory, patch and test PHP, Node.js and self-managed GitLab deployments hit by this week’s critical RCE flaws, then open 1 PR per repo. The post Cognition Open-Sources an Agent Plugin that Helps Secure Systems against Recent Cybersecurity Threats appeared first on MarkTechPost.

highlights.title: Nanbeige Releases Nanbeige4.3-33B, a 33B Open Agentic Coding Model
highlights.contentSnippet: Nanbeige LLM Lab released Nanbeige4.3-33B, a 33B dense Apache 2.0 model with 512K context. It reports 80.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and will teach the upcoming Nanbeige4.3-3B. The post Nanbeige Releases Nanbeige4.3-33B, a 33B Open Agentic Coding Model appeared first on MarkTechPost.

highlights.title: Hugging Face Releases Carbon-X, a 14B Open DNA Language Model that Brings DNA and Natural Language Together for the First Time
highlights.contentSnippet: Hugging Face released Carbon-X, an open 14.8B DNA language model built on Qwen3-14B. It reads raw DNA in chat, answers in English, and averages 66.7% across 5 DNA benchmarks under Apache 2.0. The post Hugging Face Releases Carbon-X, a 14B Open DNA Language Model that Brings DNA and Natural Language Together for the First Time appeared first on MarkTechPost.

highlights.title: PyTorch Conference 2026: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU for Native PyTorch on TPUs
highlights.contentSnippet: Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, at PyTorch Conference North America 2026, and Meta said it plans to move larger LLM workloads onto TPUs with it. AWS released TorchNeuron for Trainium the same week, while developers questioned TPU availability and where vendor lock-in now sits. By Andrew Hoblitzell

highlights.title: Google ML Drift Accelerates On-Device AI Inference Across Diverse GPUs
highlights.contentSnippet: Google has released ML Drift, an open-source, cross-platform GPU compute engine designed for on-device AI and machine learning inference. Licensed under Apache 2.0, it abstracts the complexities of different GPU hardware and low-level APIs, supporting OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal, and WebGPU. By Sergio De Simone

highlights.title: Microsoft Open-Sources Agensh: A Multi-Agent Harness for 1,024 Agents
highlights.contentSnippet: Microsoft Research open-sourced Agensh, a multi-agent harness with no central orchestrator. Self-organizing workers share a Git repo, chat and a findings board, scaling from 1 to 1,024 agents on ProgramBench under a 6-hour budget. The post Microsoft Open-Sources Agensh: A Multi-Agent Harness for 1,024 Agents appeared first on MarkTechPost.

highlights.title: Google Optimizes Agent Development Kit's 200K-line Python Codebase Overnight with Gemini 4 Argon
highlights.contentSnippet: Google explained how an 11-hour unattended run of Gemini 4 Argon produced two accepted optimizations for Google Agent Development Kit's codebase, reducing in-memory session-preparation overhead by about 40% in long sessions and cold package import time by 21%. By Sergio De Simone

highlights.title: Cognition Open-Sources an Agent Plugin that Helps Secure Systems against Recent Cybersecurity Threats
highlights.contentSnippet: Cognition released the Devin Vulnerability Fixes plugin, 3 MIT-licensed agent skills that inventory, patch and test PHP, Node.js and self-managed GitLab deployments hit by this week’s critical RCE flaws, then open 1 PR per repo. The post Cognition Open-Sources an Agent Plugin that Helps Secure Systems against Recent Cybersecurity Threats appeared first on MarkTechPost.

highlights.title: Nanbeige Releases Nanbeige4.3-33B, a 33B Open Agentic Coding Model
highlights.contentSnippet: Nanbeige LLM Lab released Nanbeige4.3-33B, a 33B dense Apache 2.0 model with 512K context. It reports 80.9 on Terminal-Bench 2.1 and will teach the upcoming Nanbeige4.3-3B. The post Nanbeige Releases Nanbeige4.3-33B, a 33B Open Agentic Coding Model appeared first on MarkTechPost.

highlights.title: Hugging Face Releases Carbon-X, a 14B Open DNA Language Model that Brings DNA and Natural Language Together for the First Time
highlights.contentSnippet: Hugging Face released Carbon-X, an open 14.8B DNA language model built on Qwen3-14B. It reads raw DNA in chat, answers in English, and averages 66.7% across 5 DNA benchmarks under Apache 2.0. The post Hugging Face Releases Carbon-X, a 14B Open DNA Language Model that Brings DNA and Natural Language Together for the First Time appeared first on MarkTechPost.

highlights.title: PyTorch Conference 2026: Google and Meta Open-Source TorchTPU for Native PyTorch on TPUs
highlights.contentSnippet: Google and Meta open-sourced TorchTPU, a native PyTorch backend for Google's TPUs, at PyTorch Conference North America 2026, and Meta said it plans to move larger LLM workloads onto TPUs with it. AWS released TorchNeuron for Trainium the same week, while developers questioned TPU availability and where vendor lock-in now sits. By Andrew Hoblitzell

highlights.title: Google ML Drift Accelerates On-Device AI Inference Across Diverse GPUs
highlights.contentSnippet: Google has released ML Drift, an open-source, cross-platform GPU compute engine designed for on-device AI and machine learning inference. Licensed under Apache 2.0, it abstracts the complexities of different GPU hardware and low-level APIs, supporting OpenGL ES, OpenCL, Metal, and WebGPU. By Sergio De Simone

highlights.title: Microsoft Open-Sources Agensh: A Multi-Agent Harness for 1,024 Agents
highlights.contentSnippet: Microsoft Research open-sourced Agensh, a multi-agent harness with no central orchestrator. Self-organizing workers share a Git repo, chat and a findings board, scaling from 1 to 1,024 agents on ProgramBench under a 6-hour budget. The post Microsoft Open-Sources Agensh: A Multi-Agent Harness for 1,024 Agents appeared first on MarkTechPost.

highlights.title: Google Optimizes Agent Development Kit's 200K-line Python Codebase Overnight with Gemini 4 Argon
highlights.contentSnippet: Google explained how an 11-hour unattended run of Gemini 4 Argon produced two accepted optimizations for Google Agent Development Kit's codebase, reducing in-memory session-preparation overhead by about 40% in long sessions and cold package import time by 21%. By Sergio De Simone
